A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MILP-Evolve study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on integrality-gap prediction, learning to branch, and language-MILP alignment, including transfer to MIPLIB and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds transfer experiments on new seed families, training-data ablations, and a GPT-4o comparison.

M1.justification: The MILP-Evolve prompt operators, parameter search and filtering, GCN/attention architecture, branching model, and training losses remain unchanged (Sections 3–4; Appendices A.1–A.2 and A.4). The added evaluations do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a distinct 50-class transfer suite evolved from six previously unused seeds: Graph Coloring, Job-Shop Scheduling, Protein Folding, Multi-Item Lot Sizing, Bin Packing, and Max Cut. Evaluation across all three existing learning tasks substantially extends coverage beyond the original MILP-Evolve and MIPLIB evaluations (Table 2; Appendix A.3.3).

E2.justification: v2 evaluates GPT-4o directly on sampled MPS files as an additional language-alignment comparator (Table 14; Appendix A.3.7). Comparator memberships in the original benchmark tables remain unchanged, including Seed, Seed + Param., and Seed + VAE.

E3.justification: Added protocols include a 40%/60% class split for fine-tuning/testing, manually checked descriptions for the new test set, single-seed and 70%/30% sampling controls, and mixture experiments fixing training/validation counts at 1200/300. The GPT-4o evaluation introduces identifier anonymization, 150-line MPS sampling, and chain-of-thought prompting. These extend evaluation design; the original benchmark settings remain intact.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3.4–A.3.5 add analyses of seed-origin proportions, training on one seed's descendants, weighted seed mixtures, and varying seed/evolved-data fractions at fixed sample counts (Tables 11–13). These directly examine dependence on training-data composition beyond the retained class-count scaling, attention ablation, structural statistics, and per-class branching analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten repeated language-task evaluations and four training repetitions for Figure 4c documented in Appendix A.1.6. Distributional summaries in v1 Table 8/v2 Table 9 are also unchanged. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 and v1 Table 2/v2 Table 3 retain their numerical results. v2 adds transfer results, including Ours' 17.98% integrality-gap deviation and 30.71% branching accuracy, plus seed/mixture ablation results. Table 14 newly reports GPT-4o's 47.79%/16.81% four-/ten-way accuracy under sampled inputs. The earlier 0.037-second attention and 0.005-second GCN timing measurements are removed.

T1.justification: The MILP and learning-task definitions, Equations (1)–(9), and histogram-similarity formulas are retained. The added application descriptions are illustrative examples, without new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central MILP-Evolve and cross-class generalization contributions remain. v2 explicitly claims the first foundation-model training approach for MILP and superiority over direct GPT-4o interpretation. It narrows the language-task framing from assisting formulation toward interpreting existing instances and removes v1's approximate million-instance headline.

C2.justification: v2 suggests filtering may explain unequal seed-generation yields and qualifies lineage statistics because crossover tracking follows only the first parent. It expands discussion of language-task applications, future description generation, and context-length limitations of direct LLM interpretation. Existing limitations concerning separate models per task and branching generalization remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a release promise with an OptiGuide code/data link, although Appendix A.1 retains the older release-on-acceptance wording. New appendices document manual label checking and the GPT-4o protocol, including 50 header, 50 random middle, and 50 tail lines and an example prompt. Original implementation details remain largely unchanged; the numerical runtime footnote is deleted.

R1.justification: Six references are added: Chen and Thizy, Jensen and Toft, Williams, Xiong et al., Raghavan and Tompson, and Ramesh et al. They support the new seed tasks and expanded rounding/generation discussion. The introduction adds an explicit priority claim, while Section 6's main positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, reorganizes contribution paragraphs, removes the separate Our Contributions subsection, expands task motivation, and adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections. The overall section sequence and most method, implementation, and prompt prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a main-text transfer table, five appendix tables covering new classes and experiments, and substantial boxed prompt, response, and description examples. It relocates v1 Figure 6 to Appendix A.3.1 as v2 Figure 11 and redistributes existing displays around the additions. This substantially expands the presentation of evidence while retaining the original figures.

improvement.justification: The new seed-family transfer suite and seed-origin/mixture controls substantially strengthen validation of the central generalization argument beyond v1's original tests. Expert-checked descriptions also improve the credibility of the new language evaluation. The GPT-4o comparison supports only its restricted 150-line input setting, and useful timing evidence is lost, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger validation of the paper's core empirical contribution.
